mammal_niche_card.name: Koala fingerprint collections
mammal_niche_card.family: A. Skin prints — fingers, palms, pads & noses
mammal_niche_card.RAW: Ink prints and SEM fingertip images from wildlife-park and university anatomy collections
mammal_niche_card.UNIT: One fingertip — one species, tens of individuals in the published study, unknown numbers in zoo/wildlife-park files, one ink-print protocol
mammal_niche_card.LABEL_GAP: Koala ridge pattern vs human prints in the same forensic reference files (the second ruler is our own fingerprint system)
mammal_niche_card.ANCHOR: The 1997 Adelaide reference prints (Henneberg, Lambert & Leigh)
mammal_niche_card.headline: A koala's fingerprint is nearly indistinguishable from a human's under a microscope — verified in 1997, and no, it has never actually turned up at a crime scene.
mammal_niche_card.why_niche: One famous study, then near-silence: wildlife parks handle koalas daily and no print collection was ever built on the 1997 foundation.
mammal_niche_card.score_justification: Headline is perfect and verified (Henneberg 1997), but the known print population is small — one species, tens of documented individuals — so archive depth caps the score.
